To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the levels of mRNA coding for the lipogenic enzymes fatty-acid synthetase, acetyl-CoA-carboxylase, ATP-citrate lyase, and malic enzyme in rat lung are not regulated by fasting, refeeding, or by development.
in the lung of the developing rat, the synthesis of lipogenic enzymes is regulated by changes in the abundance and stability of the mRNAnas encoding them.
the abundance of mRNA coding for fatty-acy synthase, acetyl-CoA, ATP citrate lyases and malic enzyme was studied in rat lung and liver.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the lipogenic pathway in the developing rat lung.
the regulation of lipogenesis in the rat lung.
the role of the lung as a metabolic organ and the control of the expression of lipogenic enzymes in this organ.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the regulation of lipogenic enzymes in lung differs from that observed in liver and that in the prenatal period of rat development, pretranslative regulation is involved in controlling the synthesis of these lipogenic enzymes.
in the rat lung the abundance of the mRNAS encoding lipogenic enzymes is controlled pre- and post-natally, whereas in the liver the regulation is post-natal only.

the abundance of mRNA for fatty acid-synthesizing enzymes in lung is regulated by different mechanisms from those regulating the abundance of mRNA in liver, and that the abundance of m-RNAs encoding lipogenic enzymes is developmentally regulated in the lung.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the regulation of lipogenic enzyme synthesis in the lung differs markedly from the regulation in the liver, that the regulation of these enzymes in the developing lung involves a complex interaction of pretranslational and post-translational events and that the regulation of fatty-acid synthetase, acetyl-CoA synthetase and ATP citrate lyse is similar in both organs.

the regulation of mRNAs for lipogenic enzymes differs between the lung and the liver, and that the abundance of mRNAS encoding these enzymes is controlled by different mechanisms in the developing lung.
the lung has a unique regulation of lipogenesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
lung fatty acid synthesis is developmentally regulated and the regulation is different from the regulation of fatty acid synthesis in the liver.

the abundance of mRNAS for the lipogenic enzymes fatty-acid synthetase, acetyl-CoA-carboxylase, ATP-citrate lyase and malic enzyme is regulated in the rat lung in a manner different from that in the rat liver.

the abundance of m-RNA for lipogenic enzymes is not regulated in the same way in lung and liver, which is consistent with previous studies showing differences in lipogenic enzyme activities in these tissues.
